runs: , a personality typology theory — we sort two MBTI types into 5 categories based on how much they overlap on perceiving (N/S) and judging (T/F) style. This doesn’t reproduce Socionics’ full official relationship system, and it’s
for predicting real relationship satisfaction — just for fun. The same MBTI pair always gives the same result (order doesn’t matter).

duality.name: Opposite & Complementary
duality.description: Opposite on both how you take in information (N/S) and how you decide (T/F). In Socionics theory, this is considered the most ideal complementary match — each person's strengths cover the other's blind spots.

perceivingAligned.name: Perceiving-Aligned
perceivingAligned.description: You take in information the same way (N/S), but decide differently (T/F). You see the world similarly but make decisions differently — that can make for interesting chemistry.

judgingAligned.name: Judging-Aligned
judgingAligned.description: You decide the same way (T/F), but take in information differently (N/S). Your decision-making style clicks, even if your interests or perspective differ.

sameFunctions.name: Similar Wiring
sameFunctions.description: You use the exact same set of mental functions — you just prioritize them differently. That tends to make it easy to understand how the other person thinks.

identity.name: Same Type
identity.description: You're the exact same type. Instant mutual understanding, but you may also share the same blind spots.
